scope: Every original event dated 2018 through 2025 inclusive

records.note: Next-day reporting supports 103 deaths and 235 wounded, not more than 235. Remove the unsupported editorial conclusion.

changes.description: On January 27, 2018, a Taliban attacker detonated explosives carried in an ambulance in central Kabul. Afghanistan's interior minister reported the next day that 103 people had been killed and 235 wounded.

records.note: Date, school, location and 17 killed/17 wounded are supported by the FBI incident record. The original nationwide student-movement claim was not established in the reviewed evidence and is omitted from the concise replacement. This verifies the replacement, not the omitted claim.

changes.description: On February 14, 2018, a gunman killed 17 people and wounded 17 others at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida.

records.note: The final 60-death figure is corroborated by 2021 court reporting. The original 41 children belongs to early 64-death reporting; later court coverage says at least 37 children. Remove the erroneous demographic combination and unestablished more-than-20-charged claim. The concise replacement does not imply that all alleged individual failures resulted in convictions.

changes.description: A fire at the Winter Cherry shopping and entertainment complex in Kemerovo, Russia, on March 25, 2018 killed 60 people, including children. Later investigations found serious fire-safety failures.

records.note: The 2023 IIT finding identifies chlorine and 43 named victims, with reasonable grounds to attribute the attack to Syrian air forces. Do not imply sarin was established.

changes.description: On April 7, 2018, a chemical attack in Douma, Syria, killed 43 named people. In January 2023, the OPCW investigation team found reasonable grounds to believe that Syrian air forces dropped two cylinders containing chlorine on residential buildings, affecting dozens more people.

records.note: 57 was an initial toll. Later reporting gives more than 60, with secondary summaries giving 69; UNAMA records 198 total civilian casualties without a fatality breakdown in the retrieved page. Exact final death count and breakdown remain unresolved; date, registration-site identity and IS attribution are supported.
UN inquiry distinguishes 189 protest deaths from 183 killed by live ammunition. May 14 toll was subsequently established as 60; same-day OCHA's 55 was preliminary.

changes.description: Israeli forces killed 60 Palestinians during demonstrations near the Gaza perimeter fence on May 14, 2018. A subsequent UN inquiry reported more than 1,100 people shot that day. Across demonstrations from March 30 through December 31, 2018, the inquiry recorded 189 Palestinian deaths, including 183 caused by live ammunition.

records.note: Sources describe a field/agricultural land, not a hillside. The final toll includes passengers who died later, not 112 immediate deaths.

changes.description: On May 18, 2018, a Boeing 737 operating for Cubana de Aviacion crashed into a field shortly after departing Havana's Jose Marti International Airport. Of the 113 people aboard, 112 died and one survived. The aircraft was operated by Mexican charter company Global Air.

records.note: June 3 eruption is established. The asserted 425 confirmed CONRED deaths is not established: reports variously combine recovered deaths and missing people, and the 2026 government-newspaper retrospective itself gives 429 dead plus 229 missing. Hundreds injured/thousands of homes destroyed also need final evidence. No numerical replacement proposed without reconciling categories.

The outbreak and humanitarian crisis are established, but July 1 is not established as an event or reporting cutoff. The 2,315 total needs its exact WHO reporting interval; this is a cumulative cholera figure, not famine deaths or deaths on July 1. The outbreak began in 2016, with a major wave in April 2017.

225 is an early reported tally; published mortality analysis gives 237. JMA documents June 28-July 8 rainfall, including cumulative totals over 1,800 mm, not the asserted 180 mm/hour. July 6 is an anchor within the disaster, not all deaths on that date. The precise July 6 calendar date remains an unestablished selection within a June 28-July 8 rainfall episode; explaining it as an anchor does not verify it as the event date.

changes.description: Heavy rainfall from late June through early July 2018 caused flooding and landslides across western Japan, especially Hiroshima, Okayama and Ehime. A published mortality analysis recorded 237 deaths, including 115 in Hiroshima Prefecture. The July 6 calendar entry falls within the multi-day disaster.

records.note: Raisani belonged to Balochistan Awami Party, not ANP. Reuters updated Mastung deaths to 149. Same-day other bombing was Bannu, killing four; Peshawar was a different attack.

changes.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Balochistan Awami Party election rally near Mastung, Pakistan, on July 13, 2018. A subsequent official tally reported by Reuters put the deaths at 149, including candidate Siraj Raisani. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

records.note: August 5 date and magnitude 7.0 per Indonesian authority supported. 563 is a sequence-wide figure in secondary accounts. Need final BNPB report for death, housing and displacement totals and especially purported tourist deaths in the Gili Islands; sources retrieved do not establish those full-record details.

Xinhua's August 14 account relays the ICRC's final information from Saada authorities: 51 dead, 40 children, 79 injured. Its full text also attributes the field-trip account to local residents. The replacement omits the unestablished UNICEF attribution and broad political consequences, rather than leaving peripheral prose unresolved. The coalition defended the strike's legitimacy at the time; that does not negate the reported civilian toll.

changes.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a school bus at Dahyan market in Saada Governorate on August 9, 2018. The ICRC relayed a local-authority tally of 51 dead, including 40 children, and 79 injured.

records.note: Over 100 dams is wrong: state-hosted case study gives 35, UNDP 37. Report intervals produce 433 versus 483 deaths. Preserve 483 only as the broader case-study tally and make multi-day scope clear. The precise August 15 calendar anchor remains unestablished within the multi-day flood period; retain the supported prose correction but withhold until the date/period representation is resolved.

changes.description: Monsoon flooding and landslides devastated Kerala in August 2018. A case study hosted by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority reports over 483 deaths and about one million evacuees, with 35 dams opened. Other assessments use different reporting intervals and totals; these deaths did not all occur on August 15.

records.note: Landfall was early September 15 local time, September 14 UTC; UTC date correction supported. 134 is a multinational total in secondary summaries, not Philippine deaths; Hong Kong deaths and 400,000 destroyed homes are not substantiated. Keep unresolved until a consistent final geographic toll and damage definition are established.

Ferry was approaching Ukara, not just departing Ukerewe. 41 survivors, not hundreds; 228 is the later government tally summarized by secondary source, while September 24 AFP still reported 224. The later 228 toll was not corroborated beyond a secondary summary in this batch; the opened contemporary AFP source still had 224. Route/survivor corrections do not establish a final death tally.

changes.description: The overloaded ferry MV Nyerere capsized while approaching Ukara Island on Lake Victoria on September 20, 2018. Later government figures put the death toll at 228, with 41 people rescued. It had been travelling from Ukerewe Island.

records.note: Date, magnitude and disaster identity supported. Need reconcile 4,340 with recovered bodies, missing and people presumed buried; calling all confirmed deaths while also listing missing risks category mixing. BNPB page returned 403 on open. Tsunami-height maximum and displacement total also require final source.
Primary institution page describes future return once completed, not completed reopening. Remove unestablished reopening assertion; attack date and toll supported.

changes.description: An antisemitic gunman attacked worshippers at Pittsburgh's Tree of Life synagogue on October 27, 2018, killing 11 people from three congregations during Shabbat services. Six others, including four police officers, were wounded. It was the deadliest antisemitic attack in United States history.

records.note: Local October 29 at about 06:33 WIB is October 28 about 23:33 UTC. Accident details support 189 aboard and prior technical issues; shorten causal narrative to retrieved evidence.

changes.description: Lion Air Flight 610, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 travelling from Jakarta to Pangkal Pinang, crashed into the Java Sea about 13 minutes after takeoff, killing all 189 aboard. It was early October 29, 2018 locally, still October 28 UTC. Investigators documented technical problems on preceding flights.

records.note: NIST and CPUC support the date, location, 85 deaths, acreage and destroyed-structure total. Omit the unestablished Paradise-specific fatality majority, home count and weather characterization; structures are not interchangeable with residential homes. The replacement's county-wide scope matches the toll.

changes.description: The Camp Fire began in Butte County, California, on November 8, 2018 and devastated Paradise and nearby communities. It killed 85 people, burned 153,336 acres and destroyed 18,804 structures.

records.note: Five attackers in total, including bomber, distinguished from four gunmen. No support for US-run hotel or targeted nearby court; remove those claims.

changes.description: Al-Shabaab attacked the DusitD2 hotel and business complex in Nairobi on January 15, 2019. Twenty-one victims were killed. Kenyan authorities said all five attackers also died. The toll of 21 excludes the attackers.

records.note: 259 identified plus 11 missing is a dated search tally, not a permanent final breakdown. Authorities and memorials also use 272 including two unborn children; retain 270 people with scope disclosed.

changes.description: Vale's Corrego do Feijao tailings dam collapsed at Brumadinho, Brazil, on January 25, 2019, killing 270 people. Local authorities and victims' families commemorate 272 victims when two unborn children are included. Identification and recovery of victims continued for years after the collapse.

records.note: Core event, date and 40 security deaths supported; clarify disputed territory as Indian-administered Kashmir and exclude bomber from count.

changes.description: A Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a convoy of Indian paramilitary police in Pulwama on February 14, 2019, killing 40 security personnel. The attack was followed by Indian airstrikes at Balakot and an aerial confrontation between India and Pakistan.

records.note: Investigation and reporting support date (05:38 UTC departure), route, six-minute flight, 157 deaths, 149 passengers/eight other personnel, multinational victims and MCAS-related worldwide grounding for nearly two years. BEA classifies the eighth non-passenger as an in-flight security officer. The original calls all eight non-passengers crew, whereas BEA separately identifies an in-flight security officer. Replace that breakdown and the generalized grounding duration with a concise supported flight account.

changes.description: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Addis Ababa to Nairobi, crashed near Bishoftu on March 10, 2019, about six minutes after takeoff. All 157 people aboard died.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science

records.note: Landfall near Beira March 14-15 established. Claimed confirmed 1,593 and 2,000 missing not established. WHO gives 603 for Mozambique; an EM-DAT-based study gives 1,234 storm deaths. Need consistent multinational period and missing-versus-dead accounting before replacement.

The Royal Commission establishes the date, two mosque locations and 51 murders. Forty attempted-murder charges are not by themselves proof of precisely 40 injuries. Remove that numeric injury claim, the unestablished livestream detail and ancillary legislative aftermath from the concise replacement; the omitted claims are not certified.

changes.description: A gunman attacked the Al Noor Mosque and Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand, on March 15, 2019, killing 51 people.

records.note: UN investigation establishes at least 157, versus initial 134; 160 not established by these primary sources. Attribute perpetrators to investigation rather than treating all Dogon people as responsible.

changes.description: Armed men attacked the Fulani part of Ogossagou village in central Mali at about 05:00 on March 23, 2019. A UN investigation concluded that at least 157 people were killed. It identified most attackers as traditional hunters, accompanied by men in military and civilian clothing.

records.note: 1,000 is an interim toll. The offensive ended through military withdrawal in June, before the later ceasefire; final death count remains unresolved.

Date and coordinated church/hotel attack supported. 269 excluding nine bombers is in secondary summaries, while initial official counts were sharply revised. Need primary/reputable final total and confirmation of all location/injury/attribution details; do not substitute the preliminary 359 or 250-260.

Search supports campaign identity and reports 1,043 civilians in secondary coverage. Need the underlying SOHR final interval and combatant total, UN source for 500 deaths, and distinction between April air campaign and subsequent ground offensive. Not verified from secondary summaries.

June 3 attack and RSF involvement supported. Amnesty distinguishes at least 100 in its estimate, 127 from Central Committee of Sudanese Doctors, 50 from a different doctors' syndicate, and 87 from attorney-general inquiry. Original 104/128 attribution conflates organizations and reporting intervals; exact canonical tally remains unresolved.

Confirmed national record is 46.0 C at Verargues June 28, not 45.9 C at Gallargues. The French mortality bulletin covers both June and July heatwaves. No identifiable peer-reviewed study supporting the claimed Europe-wide 2,500 total retrieved; replacement death scope must be settled before integration.

Search did not establish a July 2019 Majiya explosion killing 48. Primary investigation notice and AFP locate the major Majiya disaster on October 15, 2024 with much higher deaths. Likely conflation, but failed search alone is not proof of fabrication. Quarantine pending identity/date resolution; do not silently repurpose as 2024.

Reuters supports more than 1,600 rain-related deaths since June by October 1, 2019, not deaths on July 1. Seasonal date anchor and displacement/geographic/detail claims remain incompletely supported. Needs a reporting cutoff rather than single-day presentation. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

Sentencing, victim targeting and toll supported. Replace unsupported arrested-at-scene detail and clarify actual charges as hate crimes/firearms rather than implying a specific domestic-terrorism criminal count.

changes.description: A gunman targeting Hispanic shoppers attacked the Cielo Vista Walmart in El Paso, Texas, on August 3, 2019. Twenty-three people died and 22 were injured. The attacker pleaded guilty to federal hate-crime and firearms charges and was sentenced in July 2023 to 90 consecutive life terms.

records.note: September 1 landfall, category 5 and 185 mph established. Need reconcile 84 all-area deaths and 74 Bahamas with NHC confirmed/reported and missing categories and later Bahamas revisions; no full verification of numeric death/displacement scope. The NHC report could not be opened successfully (access denied), so its final mortality table was not checked.

Government white paper gives 91 dead, three missing, 42 seriously and 334 lightly injured as of April 10, 2020. About 100 may reflect later indirect deaths; source for that basis absent. Need consistent final interval and source for 70 rivers/world-cup/superlative claims. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.
Official early toll is 74; later accounts sometimes 75. Inquiry reporting disputes simple cooking-cylinder explanation. Early morning 06:30 Pakistan is 01:30 UTC, same date.

changes.description: The Karachi-to-Rawalpindi Tezgam Express caught fire near Rahim Yar Khan at about 06:30 local time on October 31, 2019. Radio Pakistan reported 74 deaths that day. Later inquiry reporting identified a possible electrical short circuit followed by cylinder explosions.

records.note: Core toll supported; remove broad 'without warning' and incompletely checked nationality/legal assertions. Sudden eruption is not evidence of no prior hazard warning.

changes.description: Whakaari/White Island erupted in New Zealand's Bay of Plenty on December 9, 2019, while visitors and guides were on the island. Twenty-two people died and 25 were injured, most critically. Two victims' bodies were not recovered.

records.note: 85 appears in later secondary totals. A second bus-station blast is not established and may conflate a different bombing. Need final reputable toll and responsibility statement.

377 mm daily rainfall and 397,171 displaced reported. Exact onset requires UTC conversion: early January 1 local is December 31 UTC. No primary final 66-death tally, 60,000 residual-displacement cutoff or full water-depth/rivers support retrieved. Retain unresolved rather than selecting an arbitrary onset time.

89 soldiers supported by Reuters security sources, while France confirms fighter-jet response; do not attribute the casualty count directly to French army or treat affiliation as independently established.

changes.description: Militants attacked Niger's military post at Chinagodrar near the Mali border on January 9, 2020. Reuters subsequently reported that at least 89 Nigerien soldiers were killed. French fighter jets were sent to help repel the attackers.

records.note: 29 victims were killed across multiple sites, not all inside the mall. Total 30 includes perpetrator. Historical superlative must be time-qualified. Set lives_lost to 29 victims consistently with other attack entries; 30 includes the perpetrator.

changes.description: On February 8-9, 2020, a Thai soldier killed 29 people in a rampage in Nakhon Ratchasima that included a military base and Terminal 21 shopping mall. He was killed by security forces after an overnight siege, bringing the total including the attacker to 30. It was Thailand's deadliest mass shooting at the time.

records.note: Nine is the racist public-attack victim count, excluding the perpetrator's mother; all murders described total ten. Propose explicit victim scope and avoid suicide method details.

changes.description: On February 19, 2020, a racist attacker killed nine people of immigrant backgrounds at sites in Hanau, Germany. He also killed his mother and died by suicide. Ten victims were killed; the perpetrator's death is excluded from this count. Authorities treated the attack as far-right terrorism.

records.note: 33/34 official tallies vary, with later reports higher. Russian involvement is disputed rather than established. Must distinguish March 5 ceasefire agreement from its March 6 effective time and establish actual strike location/building versus convoy with primary/reputable reporting.

sources.name: India National Centre for Disease Control

records.note: 02:30-03:00 May 7 IST is May 6 UTC. Supported UTC correction; exact final death count and attribution to NDRF, hospitalization counts and sealed-tank wording require further final-source reconciliation.

sources: India National Centre for Disease Control

records.note: MSF identifies Dasht-e-Barchi hospital rather than Ataturk Children's Hospital; updated injury toll exceeds 20. Remove unestablished uniforms, nationality of responding forces and attribution details.

changes.description: Gunmen attacked the MSF-supported maternity wing of Dasht-e-Barchi hospital in Kabul on May 12, 2020. Afghan authorities reported 24 people killed and more than 20 injured. MSF subsequently confirmed that the dead included 16 mothers, one MSF midwife and two children aged seven and eight.

records.note: May 20 landfall supported. Landfall winds were 155-165 km/h, gusting 185, not 260; 260 confuses peak offshore strength with landfall. 103+26 does not sum to 133 and remaining country scope is absent. Need final reconciled toll; first Bay-of-Bengal super-cyclone-since-1999 claim also needs authoritative check.
Later reporting gives 28 deaths, versus 27 in early charging report. Facility named Recuperando mi Vida, not original name.

changes.description: Three armed men attacked the Recuperando mi Vida rehabilitation centre in Irapuato, Guanajuato, on July 1, 2020. Later reporting put the death toll at 28. The killings occurred amid a series of attacks on rehabilitation centres in the state.

records.note: HRW's August 2021 investigation supports the date, port, ammonium nitrate, 218 deaths and 7,000 wounded. The original strictly 'over 7,000' is stronger than the source; use an approximate count. The correction removes no contradictory death evidence retrieved in this batch.

changes.description: An ammonium nitrate explosion at the Port of Beirut on August 4, 2020 killed 218 people and wounded about 7,000, according to Human Rights Watch's investigation.

records.note: Landfall identity and category supported; 81 is a combined direct/indirect total, not Louisiana fatalities. Louisiana government cites 31 rather than original 30; sources vary on Dominican Republic and Louisiana breakdowns. Need final NHC mortality table and check 'strongest since 1856' against 1856/2020 intensity equivalence.

September 27 start and 44-day war supported. Official counts have continued changing; latest retrieved Armenian report gives 3,833 including 3,755 military and 78 civilians. 6,900 needs matching as-of dates and inclusion policy for missing/foreign fighters, not a mixture of rounded figures. Mortality study estimates are not official named deaths.

Date and IS attack supported. Sources differ between 22 initially, 35 students/professors in later reporting, and secondary 32 victims plus three attackers. Do not infer 32 by subtracting attackers from a source saying 35 students/professors. Iranian book-fair context and over-50 injured require corroboration.

Hurricane/date identity established; retrieved summaries disagree internally between at least 175 and 189. Need final NHC table and national figures to reconcile missing, presumed dead and Eta-versus-Iota totals; 74 Honduras/60 Guatemala/19 Panama breakdown not established.

Secondary summaries cite Reuters' 767 but direct Reuters investigation was not retrieved. Must distinguish November 9 killings of Amhara civilians from subsequent retaliatory killings of Tigrayans. Original attribution to Amnesty and 1,100 upper estimate require source-specific scope; not independently verified.

November 11 Philippine landfall supported. Secondary accounts conflict between 102 dead/10 missing, 98/19 and 101/10 at different dates. Need NDRRMC final report and distinguish affected from displaced; one million displaced is not established.
10 patients killed established; immediate official reporting gives seven critically injured rather than four. Remove unestablished syringe-pump cause.

changes.description: A fire broke out in the COVID-19 intensive-care unit of Piatra Neamt Emergency Hospital in Romania on November 14, 2020. Ten patients died, and officials initially reported seven people critically injured, including a doctor. Firefighters reported extinguishing the blaze in about 25 minutes.

records.note: UN's initial 110 figure was amended to tens. The primary statement confirms November 28 attack and abductions, not precise totals. Six injured, 15 women abducted and the alleged precipitating dispute remain unestablished; no defensible exact replacement toll.

Attack followed landing, rather than necessarily occurring during landing. UN missile analysis must not be reduced to unqualified attribution without checking confidence language. Early Reuters toll was 22; 28/107 later secondary tally and Saudi ambassador aboard require final evidence.

UTC origin is January 14 at 18:28, not January 15. 105 appears in secondary summaries; months of aftershocks hampering rescue is not established. Propose only supported UTC correction pending full final-toll and recovery evidence.

Primary December 6 briefing reports 1,303 killed and 7,796 currently detained. Year-end more-than-1,400 and over-10,000 need December 31 evidence and a distinction between all arrested and still detained. These are cumulative post-coup deaths, not February 1 deaths. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

sources.name: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

records.note: Scientific reconstruction identifies rock and glacier ice from Ronti Peak, not simply Nanda Devi glacier breaking off. About 200 is dead-and-missing, not 200 recovered/confirmed bodies. A combined killed-or-missing estimate cannot establish 200 deaths for the lives_lost field. Retain the supported avalanche mechanism but withhold until a death-only or legally presumed-dead count is supported.

changes.title: Chamoli rock and ice avalanche
changes.description: A massive rock and ice avalanche from Ronti Peak caused the Chamoli disaster in Uttarakhand on February 7, 2021. Debris swept down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga valleys and damaged two hydropower projects. Roughly 200 people were killed or remained missing; this is a combined dead-and-missing estimate.
sources: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

sources.name: Texas Department of State Health Services

records.note: 246 is the state's broad February winter-storm total, including deaths through June and multiple weather episodes; not necessarily all caused by a single storm starting February 13. 158 hypothermia deaths supported. The broader February winter-weather total is supported, but February 13 is not established as the start date of that matched scope. A specific storm-name/date cannot silently stand in for several weather episodes.

changes.description: Severe winter weather and power failures left millions of Texans without essential services in February 2021. Texas health officials ultimately identified 246 storm-related deaths, including 158 from hypothermia. The total covers deaths from February 11 through June 4, including later deaths linked to the disaster, rather than deaths on February 13 alone.
sources: Texas Department of State Health Services
changes.title: Texas winter-weather disaster, February 2021

records.note: AP's later court reporting corroborates all eight victims across the three businesses and six Asian women. The concise replacement omits arrest-timing and broad national-response claims. The shooter denied a racial motive, while Fulton prosecutors sought a hate-crime sentencing enhancement; neither position is silently converted into a final motive finding.

changes.description: A gunman attacked three Atlanta-area massage businesses on March 16, 2021, killing eight people, including six women of Asian descent.

records.note: Affidavit identifies an AR-style semiautomatic pistol, not simply a rifle; remove unestablished mental-health/purchase causal implication.

changes.description: A gunman killed ten people, including police officer Eric Talley, at the King Soopers supermarket in Boulder, Colorado, on March 22, 2021. Police captured the suspect alive. An arrest affidavit said he purchased a Ruger AR-556 semiautomatic pistol on March 16, six days before the attack.

records.note: 400,000 appears to conflate a cumulative pandemic milestone with calendar-2021 deaths and with the April-June wave. The later study estimates 2.4 million excess deaths in 2021 at 7.2 times reported COVID deaths, inconsistent with 400,000 as the annual official count. April 1 is not established as a discrete event date; do not replace reported deaths with excess mortality without changing scope.
Approximately 22:22-22:25 May 3 in Mexico City is May 4 UTC. Sources report 79 injured rather than about 70; avoid overstating final investigation findings from secondary summaries.

changes.description: An elevated section of Mexico City Metro Line 12 collapsed beneath a train between Olivos and Tezonco late on May 3, 2021 local time, May 4 UTC. Twenty-six people died and 79 were injured.

records.note: 256 is Gaza-only, while record title/location and description include Israel. Same-cutoff Palestinian/Israeli totals must be reconciled before choosing a combined integer; original description's 256+13 is 269. Counts also revised after ceasefire. Start May 10 supported, not all deaths on that day.
Solhan attack began around 02:00 June 5, local time equals UTC. June 4 can conflate preceding Tadaryat attack. 160 was a provisional reported toll, while official/UNICEF figure exceeded 130.

changes.description: Armed attackers struck Solhan in Burkina Faso early on June 5, 2021, killing civilians including children and forcing residents to flee. Contemporary reporting put the provisional toll at about 160; UNICEF reported more than 130 civilian deaths. The larger number is a reported estimate, not a reconciled final count.

records.note: IPC explicitly says evidence did not support area-level Famine classification; household Catastrophe is different. 190,000 is not a measured June 2021 famine toll. Underlying Ghent estimate, cause categories, November 2020-June 2022 interval and 'most during 2021' require original study; do not label estimate a UN-declared famine's deaths.
98 victims were occupants, not necessarily all residents. Investigation remains ongoing on retrieved NIST pages; avoid implying a completed causal determination.

changes.description: The 12-storey Champlain Towers South condominium in Surfside, Florida, partially collapsed at about 01:30 local time on June 24, 2021, killing 98 people. NIST opened a technical investigation into the collapse.

records.note: June 25-July 1 period, Lytton 49.6 C on June 29 and 619 heat-related BC deaths established. More than 800 investigated BC deaths is not the same as heat-attributed deaths. Need independent US/other-Canada totals and interval to substantiate combined about-800 figure and household demographics.

July event/weather mechanisms supported. Final geographic death totals vary across updates: secondary totals reach 243 including 196 Germany, not 189. Need primary final country breakdown and attribution study before replacing broad 240 estimate.

398 includes dead and missing across July 17-23, 95.5% (380) in Zhengzhou. Subway deaths were 14, not dozens. 302 is an earlier provincial figure wrongly assigned to Zhengzhou. The reported combined category does not establish 398 confirmed deaths. Withhold the numeric deaths-bearing row until missing-versus-dead accounting is resolved; the July 20 Zhengzhou flooding itself is established.

changes.description: Torrential rains struck Henan from July 17 to 23, 2021, with severe flooding in Zhengzhou on July 20. A subsequent State Council investigation recorded 398 people dead or missing across the province, 380 of them in Zhengzhou. Fourteen people died in the subway flooding. The 398 figure is a combined dead-and-missing toll.

records.note: 2,207 was preliminary. IFRC retrospective gives 2,248 deaths and 12,763 injured; UTC date remains August 14 at 12:29.

changes.description: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck southwestern Haiti on August 14, 2021, destroying thousands of homes and damaging infrastructure. The IFRC subsequently reported 2,248 deaths and 12,763 injuries. These are later reported totals, rather than the initial rescue-period count.

records.note: US investigation establishes a single bomber, not a second explosion as part of the attack. 183 combines 13 troops and approximately 170 Afghans, so is approximate.

changes.description: An ISIS-K suicide bomber attacked crowds at Kabul airport's Abbey Gate on August 26, 2021, during evacuation operations. Thirteen US service members and around 170 Afghan civilians were killed. The subsequent US military investigation described one bomber, correcting early reports of a complex attack.

records.note: Initial more-than-100 was killed AND injured in UNAMA reporting; later UNAMA report documents at least 80 dead and 150 wounded. An initial UNAOC release also repeated 100 killed, underscoring preliminary disagreement.

changes.description: A suicide bomber attacked the Sayed Abad Shia mosque in Kunduz on October 8, 2021. A later UNAMA report recorded at least 80 people killed and at least 150 wounded. Early reports used conflicting casualty figures, including a combined dead-and-injured total above 100.

records.note: NWS assessment supports 89 direct tornado deaths and 71 tornadoes across eight states, not six. 89 is entire-outbreak toll, not one Mayfield tornado. Need UTC beginning of chosen whole-outbreak scope; Mayfield's late December 10 local impact is December 11 UTC.
405 is a reported tally, not 'more than 405'; early NDRRMC table distinguishes validated and still-being-validated reports. Remove unsupported combined late impact counts.

changes.description: Typhoon Rai, known in the Philippines as Odette, struck the country on December 16, 2021, causing destructive winds, flooding and displacement. Philippine disaster reporting recorded 405 reported deaths. Initial situation reports included fatalities still undergoing validation.

key.title: Horn of Africa drought and hunger crisis

records.note: 43,000 is modeled excess mortality in Somalia across all 2022, not a January 1 event or Horn-wide confirmed famine toll. Commissioned by WHO/UNICEF, with FAO support; no area-level famine declaration implied. January 1 is a study-year boundary, not an established discrete disaster date. The annual mortality estimate is supported, but the current calendar record needs a justified period representation before publication.

changes.title: Somalia drought: estimated excess deaths in 2022
changes.description: A study commissioned by WHO and UNICEF and released in March 2023 estimated approximately 43,000 excess deaths associated with Somalia's drought during January-December 2022, about half among children younger than five. January 1 marks the start of the study year, not the date these deaths occurred; the total is an estimate rather than a confirmed count.

records.note: 231 was February 28 tally with five missing. Later disaster study reports 233 deaths.

changes.description: Extreme rainfall caused catastrophic flooding and landslides in Petropolis, Brazil, on February 15, 2022. More than 250 mm fell within hours. A later disaster study recorded 233 deaths, the highest toll for a disaster in the city's history.

records.note: 6,919 is an early-January-2023 verification snapshot, not current final 2022 total. Keep source cutoff explicit; overlaps original March 24 'start' record that maintainer should deduplicate.

changes.description: Russia began its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. By early January 2023, UN human rights monitors had verified at least 6,919 civilian deaths since the invasion, while warning the actual toll was higher. This is a dated cumulative civilian count and excludes military deaths; it is not a count of deaths on February 24.

records.note: Next-day toll reached 63 victims; five police deaths and including attacker are unsupported. Earlier contemporaneous figures were 57/62. Concise replacement avoids unsupported breakdown.

changes.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani Bazaar area during Friday prayers on March 4, 2022. Reporting the next day put the death toll at 63 after injured victims died. Islamic State's regional affiliate claimed responsibility.

key.title: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crash

records.note: Preliminary absence of identified abnormalities is not proof of no mechanical failure or crew error. Replace with actual investigation limit; March 21 local afternoon remains March 21 UTC.

changes.description: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735, a Boeing 737-800 travelling from Kunming to Guangzhou, descended rapidly and crashed near Wuzhou, Guangxi, on March 21, 2022. All 132 people aboard died. The April 2022 preliminary investigation did not determine the cause; debris examination and flight-data analysis were continuing.

key.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine — Start of Full-Scale War

records.note: Full-scale invasion began February 24, not March 24. Duplicates original February 24 invasion record. 100,000 lacks date, civilian/military definition and source; possible confusion of casualties with deaths. Merge/remove decision belongs to maintainer; do not apply date correction without duplicate review.

Municipal 458 includes 39 apparently natural deaths and one bag of remains; not 458 established unlawful killings. OHCHR records 422 bodies recovered by September and 73 documented civilian killings during March 4-30. April 2 is discovery/reporting period, not killing date. Wider 1,300 appears Kyiv-region rather than town-specific and attribution needs correction; retain contradictory denominators.

sources.name: South Africa Department of Water and Sanitation

records.note: 435 is supported as May 3 reported toll, with 63 missing, not a timeless final number. Remove unneeded historical superlative. April 11 remains an unestablished selection within the multi-day episode in the evidence reviewed; the dated May 3 mortality report does not establish that event date.

changes.description: Heavy rain and flooding devastated KwaZulu-Natal, including Durban, in April 2022. On May 3, the provincial government reported 435 deaths and 63 people still missing. Homes, roads, bridges and water infrastructure were extensively damaged. April 11 anchors the multi-day flooding episode.
sources: South Africa Department of Water and Sanitation

records.note: Core event/toll and completed state sentencing established. Replace peripheral livestream/context with concise core; state judgment does not resolve separate federal prosecution.

changes.description: A white supremacist gunman attacked a Tops supermarket in Buffalo, New York, on May 14, 2022, killing ten Black people and injuring three others. He later pleaded guilty to state charges and received life imprisonment without parole.

records.note: 21 victims, not 22; 22 includes the attacker. DOJ measures 77 minutes from initial officers' arrival to confrontation, not a generic initial entry.

changes.description: A gunman killed 19 children and two teachers at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, on May 24, 2022. A US Justice Department review found a 77-minute gap between officers first arriving and confronting and killing the attacker. The victim count excludes the attacker.

key.title: BM Container Depot fire and explosions (Sitakunda)

records.note: June 4 fire established. Initial 49 was explicitly corrected to 41 after a miscount; later secondary sources say at least 47. Need eventual reconciled death tally rather than reinstating erroneous initial total. More-than-450 injured and explosion-distance details also not established.

1,739 is a retrospective national total, not the toll on the June start date. UNICEF repeats the one-third-underwater claim, but mapped inundation summarized in the secondary source is substantially smaller; remove this disputed extent and unverified injury/climate details rather than assert them. June 14 is the flood-period anchor, not a one-day disaster. The exact June 14 onset anchor was not corroborated beyond the secondary summary; UNICEF establishes the June-to-seasonal disaster, not this precise day.

changes.description: Monsoon flooding in Pakistan beginning in June 2022 affected more than 33 million people. UNICEF's retrospective reporting records 1,739 deaths and more than 2.2 million homes damaged or destroyed across the flood-affected areas.

records.note: 01:24 local June 22 corresponds to June 21 UTC. USGS revised magnitude is 6.0, whereas the UN retrospective uses 5.9 and other agencies used 6.1/6.2. UN annual report estimates 1,036 deaths and 2,924 injuries; WHO's June 28 snapshot had 3,669 injuries. Attribute the selected retrospective count, not a universal final toll; remove uncorroborated landslide/child details.

changes.description: An earthquake struck Khost and Paktika in southeastern Afghanistan at 20:54 UTC on June 21, 2022, early June 22 locally. USGS lists magnitude 6.0. The UN's 2022 results report estimated 1,036 deaths, 2,924 injuries and damage to at least 4,500 homes.

records.note: Seven victims and the July 4 attack are established. Forty-eight attempted-murder counts should not automatically be treated as an exact wounded-person count. Replace charging and purchase details with a concise historical description; this does not verify the original legal-purchase assertion or current court outcome.

changes.description: A gunman opened fire from a rooftop during the Independence Day parade in Highland Park, Illinois, on July 4, 2022, killing seven people and injuring dozens. Prosecutors subsequently brought 117 charges, including 21 first-degree murder counts covering the seven victims.

records.note: 61,672 is a modeled summer estimate for May 30-September 4, not a July 15 toll. The first study's annual estimate was 62,862; the later paper inferred 70,066 for the whole year, not an interchangeable revised summer count. Use the defined study-period start and omit unresearched national temperature records. May 30 is the documented study-interval start, not a verified discrete heat-disaster date. The corrected estimate and interval are supported, but the single-day calendar representation needs resolution before publication.

changes.description: A Nature Medicine study estimated 61,672 heat-related deaths across 35 European countries between May 30 and September 4, 2022, with a 95% confidence interval of 37,643-86,807. A later methodological study inferred roughly 70,066 deaths for the full year, a different time scope. These are statistical estimates, not individually confirmed deaths.

records.note: NEMA's January 2023 retrospective supersedes 603: 662 deaths, 3,174 injuries and 2,430,445 displaced. September 1 is not established as onset of the season-long floods; a precise event date remains unresolved. Remove unsupported destroyed-home total and overly simple dam-release causation.

changes.description: Flooding across Nigeria in 2022 killed 662 people, injured 3,174 and displaced about 2.43 million, according to NEMA's director general in January 2023. These are nationwide seasonal totals, not deaths on a single September day.

records.note: September 5 UTC and 93 deaths are supported; Red Cross dates that count to September 11 with missing persons separate. Magnitudes vary by scale/revision. The exact road-worker death breakdown and 600,000 affected were not established and are omitted.

changes.description: An earthquake struck Luding County in Sichuan, China, on September 5, 2022, triggering landslides and damaging buildings and roads. The Hong Kong Red Cross reported 93 deaths, more than 400 injured and 25 missing as of September 11; later landslide research reports 424 injuries.

records.note: Later UN reporting gives 54 killed and 114 wounded, replacing interim 53/about 110. Responsibility reporting conflicts: the June 2023 Dutch report says unclaimed, whereas the later UN report says ISIL-K claimed it. Do not erase this discrepancy or state an unqualified attribution. Exam detail is omitted in concise replacement.

changes.description: A suicide bombing at the Kaaj education centre in Kabul's Dasht-e Barchi district on September 30, 2022 killed 54 people and wounded 114, according to later UN reporting. Most victims were young Hazara women and girls. A later UN report attributes a claim of responsibility to ISIL-K, although an earlier Dutch government report described the attack as unclaimed.

records.note: Date, 159 deaths and 196 injuries are supported. Omit the unestablished direction-of-surge reconstruction and age generalization; police investigation supports institutional negligence. October 29 local evening is also October 29 UTC.

changes.description: A crowd crush in a narrow, sloping alley in Seoul's Itaewon district during Halloween celebrations on October 29, 2022 killed 159 people and injured 196. Police subsequently referred 23 officials to prosecutors over alleged failures in prevention and emergency response.

records.note: Health minister's November 1 count was 121 dead, 333 injured and 10 missing, not necessarily a final count. VOA reports an official identifying the second device as a motorcycle-trailer bomb, contradicting two car bombs. Use vehicle bombings and remove unsupported demographic/superlative details.

changes.title: Mogadishu twin vehicle bombings
changes.description: Two vehicle bombs exploded near Somalia's Education Ministry in Mogadishu on October 29, 2022. On November 1 the health minister reported 121 deaths, 333 injuries and ten people missing. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. An official told VOA that the second device was carried by a motorcycle pulling a trailer.

records.note: Final report directly establishes date, route, aircraft, 68 passengers plus four crew and probable cause. It calls inadvertent condition-lever movement the most probable cause, not a categorical finding about both pilots. Omit the unresearched historical superlative and visual characterization.

changes.description: Yeti Airlines Flight 691, an ATR 72-500 flying from Kathmandu, crashed on approach to Pokhara on January 15, 2023, killing all 68 passengers and four crew. Nepal's final investigation identified inadvertent movement of both condition levers to the feathered position as the most probable cause, resulting in loss of thrust, an aerodynamic stall and ground impact.

records.note: 10:22 p.m. January 21 PST is January 22 UTC. Eleven victims exclude the attacker. Concise replacement removes the unresearched superlative. The county medical-examiner page mistakenly says late January 22 locally; city memorial and contemporary timeline support January 21 local.

changes.description: A gunman attacked Star Ballroom Dance Studio in Monterey Park late on January 21, 2023 local time, January 22 UTC, killing eleven people and wounding nine. The attack occurred during Lunar New Year celebrations. He subsequently entered another dance hall in Alhambra, where he was disarmed, and later died by suicide.

records.note: 84 is the revised police count after duplicate registrations, not the initial 100/101 still repeated in some later reports. A commander claimed responsibility but TTP's spokesman denied involvement; police later attributed it to Jamaat-ul-Ahrar. Remove unsupported retaliation-for-military-operations assertion and exact injury total.

changes.description: A suicide bombing inside the Police Lines mosque in Peshawar on January 30, 2023 killed 84 people in the revised police count, mostly police personnel. A TTP commander claimed responsibility, but the group's spokesman denied involvement. Pakistani investigators later attributed the attack to Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a TTP faction.

records.note: February 6 UTC is correct, but original country subtotals do not sum to 59,000. EEFIT gives 62,013 (53,537 Turkey plus 8,476 Syria); secondary compilation also records a lower Syrian count of 5,951. A defensible harmonized cross-border confirmed total and cutoff remain unresolved. Avoid selecting one exact total without reconciling Syrian coverage; 04:17 is local, 01:17 UTC.

57 and February 28 local/UTC are established. A 2025 investigation identified human error plus obsolete infrastructure and systemic failures, so a human-error-only account is incomplete. Omit passenger count and student-holiday detail not separately established.

changes.description: A passenger train and a freight train collided head-on near Tempe, Greece, late on February 28, 2023, killing 57 people. A 2025 safety investigation identified human error, outdated infrastructure and systemic railway failures. The crash triggered widespread protests over railway safety.

records.note: April 15 is the outbreak date, not the date of all recorded deaths. December publication covers reporting through November 24: more than 12,190 reported political-violence deaths since April 15, not an exact full-2023 total. ACLED excludes indirect deaths and is incomplete. Remove unverified seven-million year-end internal-displacement claim.

changes.description: War between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces began on April 15, 2023. In its update covering events through November 24, ACLED recorded more than 12,190 reported political-violence deaths since the outbreak. This is a dated, incomplete reported-death count excluding indirect mortality, not a final toll of the war.

records.note: MONUSCO's later May appeal reports 438 deaths and over 5,000 missing; UNICEF's earlier May 13 figure was over 400 dead and 2,500 missing. Update numeric field to match the supported later reported toll; missing people must not be counted as confirmed dead. Exact final accounting remains unavailable.

changes.description: Heavy rain on May 4, 2023 triggered flooding and mudslides in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, destroying parts of Bushushu and Nyamukubi. A later MONUSCO appeal reported an official toll of 438 dead and more than 5,000 missing. The missing-person estimate is separate from confirmed deaths.

records.note: Nine includes the perpetrator; use eight victims consistently with other shooting entries. Deadliest in Texas since 2019 is false given Uvalde in 2022. Omit unnecessary attacker-biography assertions.

changes.description: A gunman killed eight people and wounded seven at Allen Premium Outlets in Allen, Texas, on May 6, 2023. A police officer who was at the mall on another call shot and killed the attacker. The eight-victim total excludes the gunman.

records.note: The Post corrected its report: the U.S. estimate covered Russian losses across Ukraine, not Bakhmut alone. Battle-specific fatalities and the claimed thousands of Ukrainian deaths remain unverified. May 20 was a Russian capture claim disputed by Ukraine; do not present it as an uncontested end date. A reliable replacement battle toll is unavailable.

Parliamentary answer gives 296 deaths, superseding interim 292. Original collision sequence is misleading: Coromandel first hit the stationary goods train. Remove unverified exact injury count and compress causal account instead of asserting an unspecified ministerial signal alteration.

changes.description: On June 2, 2023, the Coromandel Express collided with a stationary freight train near Bahanaga Bazar in Odisha, and derailed coaches struck another passenger train. India's Ministry of Railways later reported 296 deaths. The disaster prompted investigations into signaling and railway safety failures.

records.note: 42 total with 37 students is supported by the June 19 ministerial update, while earlier student subtotals differ. Most-by-machete is unsupported given dormitory burning. Uganda's Congo operations predated this attack, so remove suggestion they began in response.

changes.description: An attack blamed on Allied Democratic Forces rebels at Mpondwe-Lhubiriha Secondary School in western Uganda on June 16, 2023 killed 42 people, according to a June 19 official update, including 37 students. Attackers set a dormitory on fire; victims also suffered gunshot and machete attacks.

records.note: Later death certification increased toll from 101 to 102. Hundreds unaccounted for is a stale early-response statement. Initial ignition was August 8 UTC; the fatal afternoon spread was August 9 UTC, but the official finding of one rekindled fire supports retaining its ignition date. Remove storm-causation simplification and unresearched damage total.

changes.description: A wildfire that began near Lahaina, Maui, on the morning of August 8, 2023 local time later spread through the town. Investigators found that broken electrical lines started the fire and surviving embers rekindled in strong winds. The confirmed toll reached 102 after a later death was attributed to fire injuries in June 2024.

records.note: The quake was at 23:11 local September 8, not early that morning; UTC date remains September 8. IFRC retrospective supports 2,960 dead and over 5,600 injured. Remove unsupported through-winter shelter characterization.

changes.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Morocco's High Atlas region at 22:11 UTC on September 8, 2023, 23:11 locally. Villages in Al Haouz and surrounding areas were devastated. IFRC retrospective reporting records at least 2,960 deaths and more than 5,600 injuries.

records.note: Amnesty dates dam failure to 02:50 September 11 local (00:50 UTC). Its cited November 28 OCHA total is 4,352 for the wider Libyan flooding, not a verified city-only final count. Broaden location and explicitly state national disaster scope. Higher early figures included uncertain missing estimates and are not substituted for confirmed deaths.

changes.description: Two dams above Derna failed early on September 11, 2023 after Storm Daniel's heavy rainfall, flooding the city. OCHA's November 28 reporting recorded 4,352 deaths in the wider Libyan flood disaster, with thousands separately missing. Amnesty documented neglected dam maintenance and failures in disaster preparedness.

records.note: December 31 reported Gaza toll was 21,822 with 56,451 injured; 22,000/57,000 belongs to a later snapshot. Explicitly narrow numeric scope to Gaza in 2023, not all sides or current cumulative war deaths. Keep war origin but omit unchecked hostage total and later famine/outcome characterization. Reported count is not an independently confirmed complete civilian-only total.

changes.title: Israel-Hamas war: Gaza deaths reported in 2023
changes.description: The war began after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, followed by Israeli military operations in Gaza. By December 31, Gaza's Health Ministry reported 21,822 Palestinians killed and 56,451 injured in Gaza. This entry counts that dated Gaza total only, not deaths in Israel, later fatalities, or a final toll of the war.

records.note: WHO records 1,482 deaths and 2,100 injuries across the October 7-15 sequence; the original numeric 1,000 is an obsolete preliminary figure. Remove unsupported assertion that agencies stopped updating casualty figures. October 7 is the first quake date, not all deaths in one shock.

changes.description: A sequence of strong earthquakes struck Herat province in western Afghanistan between October 7 and 15, 2023. WHO reported 1,482 deaths and 2,100 injuries from the sequence, with widespread destruction of homes and damage to health facilities.

records.note: First calls at 18:56 EDT were still October 25 UTC. Date, 18 victims and 13 injuries supported. Body discovery after a two-day search does not establish that suicide occurred at the end of that search. Final commission report identified missed intervention opportunities. Omit unnecessary age and superlatives.

changes.description: An Army reservist killed 18 people and injured 13 at a bowling alley and a bar in Lewiston, Maine, on October 25, 2023. He was found dead after a two-day search; investigators said he died by suicide. A state commission later found that local law enforcement and the Army Reserve missed opportunities to intervene before the attacks.

sources.name: Nepal Ministry of Health and Population

records.note: 153 was a November 6 correction from 157 after duplicate names. Later government review reports 154 (101 Jajarkot, 53 Rukum West), supported by reconnaissance research. Magnitudes 5.7 moment/6.4 local are different scales, not necessarily contradictory. Remove unsupported superlative.

changes.description: An earthquake struck western Nepal at 23:47 local time, 18:02 UTC, on November 3, 2023. Nepal's health ministry review records 154 deaths across Jajarkot and Rukum West, with extensive damage to homes. Research describes the earthquake as moment magnitude 5.7, corresponding to a reported local magnitude of 6.4.
sources: Nepal Ministry of Health and Population

records.note: Event was 23:59 December 18 Beijing time, not early December 18. UTC date remains December 18. Study supports 151 fatalities and 979 injuries; some compilations list 982, so omit exact injury precision. Remove unresearched superlative and affected-person count.

changes.description: An earthquake struck Jishishan County in Gansu, China, at 23:59 local time, 15:59 UTC, on December 18, 2023. Chinese authorities measured surface-wave magnitude 6.2. The earthquake killed 151 people across Gansu and Qinghai and injured nearly 1,000.

records.note: 14 is the university-victim count, excluding attacker and three earlier murders. Core date/toll and police linkage supported. Omit unsupported field-of-study detail and superlative; distinguish university victims from wider perpetrator series.

changes.description: A student attacked Charles University's Faculty of Arts in Prague on December 21, 2023, killing 14 people and injuring 25 before dying by suicide. Police linked him to his father's killing earlier that day and to the murders of a man and infant six days earlier. Those three earlier victims are not included in this university-attack toll.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction

records.note: January 1 and magnitude 7.6 JMA are established, but 241 is an early 2024 snapshot, not the final toll. An indexed August 14, 2026 Kyodo report gives 750 across affected prefectures: 228 direct plus 522 related deaths; its full page failed to open. Need the current official table and explicit national/prefectural and direct/indirect scope before replacing the toll. Withhold rather than silently freeze an obsolete count.

Date and memorial identity are established. Early 103/95 counts were corrected to 84, then 94 by January 11; a definitive subsequent 95-person count was not established. ISIS claim is supported, but final toll requires reconciliation. The Al Jazeera evidence is used only for the later figure and claim.

Later prosecutors' count was 138, not 137; UNICEF's earlier consolidated March 2024 count was 134. Remove the unverified hectares and superlative rather than conflate broader Chilean fires with the Valparaiso disaster. February 2 is outbreak date, not a final toll date.

changes.description: Wildfires beginning on February 2, 2024 devastated communities around Vina del Mar in Chile's Valparaiso Region. Prosecutors later confirmed 138 deaths, including later fatalities, superseding lower early totals. Thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed.

key.title: Crocus City Hall Concert Hall Attack

records.note: 2025 trial reporting gives 149 killed and over 600 wounded, superseding 145/500. Retain attack date and location; shorten to supported attack narrative and claimed responsibility, without treating charges as convictions.

changes.description: Gunmen attacked Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, outside Moscow, on March 22, 2024, shooting concertgoers and setting the venue on fire. AP's August 2025 trial reporting gives 149 deaths and more than 600 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack.

records.note: June 24 national snapshot supports 315 dead, 38 missing, 188 injured and 293,205 displaced, not 291 deaths or hundreds missing. April 26 is not established as onset of this March-June seasonal event. No supported exact replacement day; withhold pending date resolution. National-disaster declaration and dam-breach claims omitted.

changes.description: Heavy seasonal rains caused floods and landslides across Kenya in 2024. UNICEF's June 24 snapshot recorded 315 deaths, 38 missing people, 188 injuries and 293,205 displaced people nationwide. These are cumulative seasonal figures, not the toll of one day in Nairobi.

sources.name: Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defense

records.note: 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing are supported retrospectively. May 1 is an emergency-declaration date, not established flood onset. IFRC dates intense rains from April 29; other accounts start April 27. Preserve this onset ambiguity rather than declare a placeholder verified. Proposed prose removes unneeded displacement precision.

changes.description: Heavy rain in late April and May 2024 caused widespread flooding in Rio Grande do Sul, including Porto Alegre. Brazil's Senate reported 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing people in its December 2024 review, with 478 municipalities affected.
sources: Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defense

records.note: 315 and over 1,600 injuries were Taliban/refugee-ministry figures, not established UN totals. UNICEF's May report gives preliminary 180 deaths/280 injuries across May 10-11 northeastern flooding; WHO gives over 180/242. Counts and geographic scopes conflict. Tens of thousands of homes is unsupported; RFE/RL cites 2,660 destroyed. Need reconciled Baghlan-specific total.

sources.name: Saudi Ministry of Municipalities and Housing

records.note: Official Hajj period is June 14-19, not a single June 15 event. Use the documented period start. WHO attributes 1,301 heat-exhaustion deaths and 83% unauthorized pilgrims to Saudi authorities; omit unverified ranking of nationalities and precise temperature.

changes.description: During the June 14-19, 2024 Hajj pilgrimage, extreme heat caused mass mortality among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia. WHO reported Saudi authorities' total of 1,301 deaths from heat exhaustion, with 83% among unauthorized pilgrims walking long distances. The toll covers the pilgrimage period, not a single day.
sources: Saudi Ministry of Municipalities and Housing

records.note: 02:17 IST July 30 is July 29 UTC. April 2025 parliamentary answer supersedes 231 recovered-body count: 298 deaths including 32 missing people legally declared dead. Body parts are not additional individuals. Remove unverified weeks-long recovery and 130-injury claim.

changes.description: Landslides struck Wayanad, Kerala, early on July 30, 2024 local time, July 29 UTC, after intense rain. A government answer to Parliament in April 2025 reported 298 deaths, including 32 missing people declared deceased, based on Kerala's official accounting.

records.note: Around 02:00 Tehran July 31 was July 30 UTC. Haniyeh and his bodyguard both died, so event toll is two. Projectile versus planted-bomb accounts conflict; do not resolve by assumption. Use mechanism-neutral killing description and omit unsupported causal effect on negotiations.

changes.description: Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh and his bodyguard were killed at a residence in Tehran around 2 a.m. on July 31, 2024 local time, July 30 UTC. Accounts differed over whether a projectile or a previously planted explosive caused the blast.

sources.name: United Nations - South Sudan famine declaration

records.note: August 1 is publication of the Zamzam famine determination, not onset of famine mortality. 61,000 is estimated all-cause mortality in Khartoum State over April 2023-June 2024, not recorded killings nationwide or famine deaths in Zamzam. First famine since 2011 is false (South Sudan 2017); a famine-specific death total is not established. Do not repurpose the unrelated mortality estimate.

The crash was about 84 minutes after departure from Cascavel, not shortly after takeoff. Date, aircraft, destination and 62 occupants are supported. Preliminary icing evidence does not alone establish cause; omit causal shorthand and unresearched historical superlative.

changes.description: Voepass Flight 2283, an ATR 72-500 flying from Cascavel to Sao Paulo-Guarulhos, crashed in Vinhedo on August 9, 2024. All 58 passengers and four crew members died. The crash occurred well into the flight, not shortly after takeoff.

records.note: Official sources establish four victims, nine injured, date and arrest. Remove unresearched annual superlative and avoid unnecessary current-court-status implication. Four felony-murder charges are a historical September 5 development.

changes.description: A 14-year-old student opened fire at Apalachee High School near Winder, Georgia, on September 4, 2024. Two students and two teachers were killed, and nine other people were injured. The suspect was taken into custody without incident and charged with four counts of felony murder.

records.note: 844 appears in Global Water Monitor but a secondary compilation ranges to 1,009; national accounting and Myanmar missing/dead reconciliation remain incomplete. September 7 is Vietnam landfall, not onset of multinational impacts. Most powerful storm of the 2024 season is not supported by HKO, which gives a narrower South China Sea ranking. Withhold pending geographic/time-scope alignment.

Date, JNIM and targets supported. AFP simultaneously reported 77 from a security source and an authenticated official document naming 81 victims and suggesting around 100. The 77 figure cannot be presented as a settled final count; civilian inclusion and exact injured total also need reconciliation.

Later IranWire reporting and parliamentary motion support 52; early AP recovered-body counts were lower with miners missing. Parliamentary motion is corroboration, not an independent technical inquiry. Remove unsupported sequential carbon-monoxide-release mechanism, precise injuries and size ranking.

changes.description: A methane explosion at the Madanjoo coal mine near Tabas, Iran, on the evening of September 21, 2024 killed 52 miners, according to later reporting. Early rescue reports gave lower recovered-body counts while other workers remained trapped.

records.note: About 4,000 was a nonfinal reported toll since October 2023, not September-November alone. Broaden entry period to actual cross-border conflict start. Pager victims were not exclusively Hezbollah members; remove that unsupported characterization. November 27 marks the 2024 ceasefire, not a permanent final outcome.

changes.title: Israel-Hezbollah conflict in Lebanon, 2023-2024
changes.description: Cross-border hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah began on October 8, 2023 and escalated sharply in September 2024. A ceasefire took effect on November 27. On November 29, the UN reported Lebanese authorities' nonfinal toll of around 4,000 dead and over 16,000 injured since the conflict began.

records.note: 232 was an earlier multi-region count, not Valencia alone. October 2025 official memorial honored 237 nationwide; RTVE identifies 229 in Valencia. Retain Valencia title/location and set 229 with explicit regional scope, mentioning national total separately. Remove stale dozens-missing claim.

changes.description: Extreme rainfall on October 29, 2024 caused flash floods in eastern Spain, especially Valencia province. By the first anniversary, 229 deaths were attributed to the disaster in Valencia and 237 across Spain. The numeric toll in this entry is Valencia's, not the nationwide total.

records.note: Core date, flight, aircraft and 179 dead/two survivors supported. Landing with gear retracted does not establish mechanical landing-gear failure. Bird evidence is documented but final causal chain should not be inferred from preliminary findings. Superlative needs geographic qualification because Korean Air 007 killed more outside Korea.

changes.description: Jeju Air Flight 2216 from Bangkok made a gear-up landing at Muan International Airport on December 29, 2024, overran the runway and struck a concrete structure. Of 181 occupants, 179 died and two survived with serious injuries. The preliminary investigation documented bird-strike evidence but did not establish the complete cause.

key.title: Israel–Hamas War: 2024 Death Toll in Gaza

records.note: December 31 OCHA publication uses Gaza MoH data through December 30: 45,541 cumulative since October 7, 2023, not 45,600 deaths during 2024. Simple difference from the 21,822 end-2023 snapshot is 23,719 but changes to cumulative reporting are not necessarily deaths occurring within the year. Need actual occurrence-year accounting or explicitly repurpose to a cumulative snapshot, avoiding double counting record 113. Annual toll remains unresolved.

UN initially documented 2,064 civilian deaths in 2024, later revised to 2,088, not about 1,300. Named Russian deaths are cumulative verified identifications, not all-side annual deaths. The exact 100,000 annual combined military total and deadliest-year assertion are not established; dynamic Mediazona data cannot be backdated to December 2024. December 31 is a reporting-period endpoint, not a one-day battle date.

key.title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack

records.note: The FBI establishes the January 1 attack, 14 victims, dozens injured and pre-attack ISIS-support videos; Reuters corroborates allegiance. Police footage establishes that Jabbar fired at officers before being killed. Fourteen excludes the attacker; the early 15-dead total included him. Early morning Central time is January 1 UTC.

key.title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)

records.note: Current incident pages report 12 Palisades and 19 Eaton civilian fatalities, and 6,845 plus 9,419 destroyed structures. These are the two named incidents, not every January California fire. January 7 is the first ignition date and January 31 the containment date, not continuous uncontrolled burning through that entire day. Palisades began 10:30 PST January 7 (18:30 UTC); Eaton began January 8 UTC. Remove unneeded ranking and wind characterization rather than leave ancillary unsupported prose.

changes.description: The Palisades and Eaton fires began in Los Angeles County on January 7, 2025 local time and were contained on January 31. CAL FIRE records 31 civilian deaths and 16,264 destroyed structures across the two fires.

key.title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja

records.note: NEMA's January 28 account gives 98 deaths and 69 injuries, not an FRSC confirmation of more than 100 recovered bodies. The early January 19 report gave 73, illustrating the reporting progression. Use 98 as a dated official report, not a claim that no later victim died. Saturday morning January 18 remains the UTC date.

changes.description: A fuel tanker accident and explosion at Dikko junction in Niger State on January 18, 2025 killed people gathered around spilled fuel. NEMA reported 98 deaths and 69 injuries in its January 28 update.

records.note: OCHA establishes that the ceasefire took effect January 19 at 11:15 local time, not its January 22 publication date, and reports hostage/prisoner releases. The 47,000 is a cumulative war toll, not deaths caused by a ceasefire; an exact matching January 19 cutoff is not established here. This overlaps the existing 2023 and 2024 Gaza death records. A later cumulative report cannot verify the number on the ceasefire date. Do not publish a deaths-bearing ceasefire row until its toll scope and duplicate treatment are resolved.

The January 21, 2026 police retrospective confirms the January 22, 2025 cafeteria murder-suicide shortly after 11 a.m., the shooter's age, ten shots in 17 seconds, one murdered student and one grazed student. The original two-death field includes the shooter. Use one victim consistently with other attack records; describe the separate perpetrator death explicitly. No UTC date rollover. AP separately reported a student's injury from a fall; the one wounded student in the replacement refers to the gunshot victim, not an assertion that no other injuries occurred.

changes.description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson shot and killed one student and wounded another in the Antioch High School cafeteria in Nashville, then died by suicide. Police reported ten shots within 17 seconds.

records.note: The February 5 UN briefing, reproduced by ANSA, supports a provisional 2,900 dead: 2,000 bodies collected from streets and 900 in morgues. This is not a final January 23-30-only total. UNICEF describes January 26-28 fighting and control of most of Goma by January 28; the January 27 UN briefing describes an ongoing battle, while the later experts' annex calls January 27 full conquest. The same report also cites narrower health-facility fatality/injury counts. The exact capture-date framing and matching casualty period remain unsettled; do not silently resolve them with publication dates.

key.title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)

records.note: NTSB records the collision at approximately 20:48 EST January 29, which is 01:48 UTC January 30. Its casualty breakdown is 60 passengers, two pilots and two flight attendants on the jet plus three helicopter crew. All 67 died. Remove the historical superlative and route-origin detail because they are unnecessary to the supported account; this is not a challenge to those omitted details.

changes.description: At about 01:48 UTC on January 30, 2025 (the evening of January 29 locally), PSA Airlines Flight 5342 and a US Army UH-60L helicopter collided near Reagan Washington National Airport and fell into the Potomac River. All 64 people on the airliner and three helicopter crew members died.

records.note: Aviation incident sources corroborate the January 29 Beechcraft 1900D flight from Unity oilfield to Juba, Eagle Air operating for Light Air Services, oil-worker transport, and 20 of 21 occupants killed. The BAAA entry gives 10:30 local time, hence January 29 UTC. Accounts differ on minutes or distance after takeoff, but the original uses only 'shortly after' and does not assert an unestablished cause.

key.title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps

records.note: The five-area finding was announced December 24, 2024 and assessed October-November conditions, with projections through May 2025. February 19 is not established as a new confirmation. Western Nuba coverage refers to residents and displaced people, not necessarily two named physical sites. A photographer's caption repeats 522,000 child malnutrition deaths attributed to the Sudan Doctors Union, but no underlying estimate, methods or authoritative corroboration was found. IPC people-in-Catastrophe figures are not deaths. The Sudan government also disputed the IPC process; its disagreement does not negate the independent famine classification. Retain in audit, not public canonical data.

changes.description: On December 24, 2024, FAO, WFP and UNICEF reported the IPC Famine Review Committee's finding of famine in at least five assessed areas, including three North Darfur displacement camps and resident and displaced populations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The assessment covered October-November 2024 and projected further spread.

records.note: The accessible Reuters methodology establishes a name-based count of 1,479 Alawites across 40 sites on March 7-9, not an exact 1,500 nor all deaths in the wider March fighting. Its investigation traces a command chain to officials alongside the new leadership. Reuters explicitly could not corroborate all other organizations' perpetrator/toll breakdowns; SNHR and SOHR used different scopes and totals. Preserve those disagreements rather than average them. Direct investigation page failed to open, but its indexed identity and Reuters methodology were accessible. Narrow the row to the documented three-day killings.

changes.description: A Reuters investigation documented 1,479 Alawites killed at 40 sites during the March 7-9, 2025 massacres in Syria's coastal region. Its reporting linked attackers through a chain of command to figures serving alongside the country's new leadership; the count does not include all deaths in the wider fighting.

records.note: The fatal flood occurred March 7, not a three-day 290-mm rainfall event. The weather service gives 290 mm in 12 hours and 312 mm over March 4-8. Identification of the last missing child in May raised the confirmed toll to 18; 17 was intermediate. NASA supports a daily rainfall record, which is narrower than the original worst-flood-in-city-history claim. Morning local time remains March 7 UTC.

changes.description: Flash flooding struck Bahia Blanca and surrounding areas on March 7, 2025, after 290 mm of rain in 12 hours. The confirmed death toll reached 18 after identification of the last missing child in May.

records.note: The military's revised count was 31 victims (23 soldiers, three railway employees, five passengers) and 33 attackers, with 354 rescued. The original 64 combines victims and perpetrators. Use 31 victims and attribute the rescue/attacker totals. BLA claimed 214 executed hostages without evidence; this contradicts the official account but is not independently verified. Early official figures were lower. The attack began March 11 around 13:00 Pakistan time; March 12 is the operation's conclusion, not its start.

changes.description: Baloch Liberation Army militants hijacked the Jaffar Express in Balochistan on March 11, 2025. Pakistan's military reported 31 victims killed, 354 hostages rescued and 33 attackers killed when the operation ended the following day.

records.note: The 2026 anniversary report cites court indictments with 63 deaths and more than 200 injuries, rather than 193. It identifies pyrotechnics, combustible ceiling foam, illegal operation and overcrowding as investigative/prosecutorial findings, not convictions. Early 59 dead does not establish that all 59 died at the scene. The 02:32 local ignition was 01:32 UTC March 16. Remove the unsupported at-scene split and qualify findings.

changes.description: A fire at the Pulse nightclub in Kocani on March 16, 2025 killed 63 people and injured more than 200, according to figures cited in court indictments. Investigators reported that pyrotechnics ignited flammable ceiling foam in a venue lacking adequate fire safety provisions.

records.note: AP dates the first fires to Friday March 21; WWA's main outbreak analysis starts March 22-23 and its April 30 summary reports 32 deaths, also used by Copernicus. Yonhap reported 31 on April 2, while WMO's later compilation cites 27 from a different source. These are not silently reconciled as an independently complete register. Use the explicitly attributed 32 March-outbreak report, not a claimed March 21-May 15 continuous event or an Andong-only toll. Remove the May endpoint and ancillary superlative.

changes.description: Wildfires began in southeastern South Korea on March 21, 2025 and spread across several areas, including Uiseong and Sancheong. World Weather Attribution's April 30 account reported 32 deaths in the March outbreak; Copernicus also reports 32 deaths and around 5,000 buildings destroyed.

records.note: The March 28 M7.7 earthquake is well supported, but 3,770 is not a final reconciled death count. Myanmar's government reported 3,782 as of August 20, 2025 for six affected regions/states; UNICEF's May 2 report used 3,835 from another reporting stream.
